question: Which event brought about a profound change in Ashoka's administrative policy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Kalinga War.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kalinga War (c. 261 BCE) brought about a profound change in Emperor Ashoka's policy. Shocked by the immense bloodshed and suffering, Ashoka gave up further wars of conquest (Bherighosha) and adopted a policy of peace, welfare and moral conquest (Dhammaghosha). (कलिंग युद्ध — अशोक की नीति में परिवर्तन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Kalinga War is described in Rock Edict XIII. After it, Ashoka embraced Buddhism and worked for the welfare of his subjects, appointing Dhamma Mahamatras to spread moral values.

• He sent missionaries, including his children Mahinda and Sanghamitta, to Sri Lanka (Ceylon).

NOTE

• Ashoka is called "Devanampiya Piyadasi" in his inscriptions. His edicts were deciphered by James Prinsep (1837).

question: Under which of the following Acts, was Warren Hastings appointed as the Governor-General of Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Regulating Act, 1773.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Regulating Act of 1773 made the Governor of Bengal the "Governor-General of Bengal", and Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General of Bengal. (रेगुलेटिंग एक्ट 1773 — वॉरेन हेस्टिंग्स)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Regulating Act was the first step by the British Parliament to control the affairs of the East India Company; it also established a Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774).

• The Charter Act of 1833 later made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India (Lord William Bentinck being the first).

NOTE

• Sequence of key Acts: Regulating Act (1773) → Pitt's India Act (1784) → Charter Acts (1793, 1813, 1833, 1853) → Government of India Act (1858, 1919, 1935).

question:
While estimating Gross Domestic Product, the monetary value of only final goods are considered because __________.

a. its immobility, the active economic flow is ended.  b. of the issues of double counting  c. the value added at each stage of the production process is included
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only b.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• While estimating GDP, only the value of final goods and services is counted (not intermediate goods) to avoid the problem of "double counting" — statement b is correct. (दोहरी गणना से बचने हेतु — केवल अंतिम वस्तुएँ)

◦ If we counted both intermediate and final goods, the same value would be added more than once.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• An alternative method that gives the same result is the value-added method, which sums the value added at each stage (this avoids double counting differently), but the question's stated reason for counting only final goods is to prevent double counting.

• GDP = the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given period.

NOTE

• Methods of measuring national income: Product/Value-added method, Income method, Expenditure method. Intermediate goods are excluded to prevent double counting.

question: The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram was built during the reign of the __________ king Narasimhavarman II.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pallava.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram), Tamil Nadu, was built during the reign of the Pallava king Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha) in the early 8th century. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. (शोर मंदिर — पल्लव राजवंश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Mahabalipuram was a major port city of the Pallavas and is famous for its rathas (monolithic temples), cave temples and rock-cut sculptures (e.g., "Descent of the Ganga / Arjuna's Penance").

• The Pallava capital was Kanchipuram.

NOTE

• The Pallavas were pioneers of Dravidian temple architecture. The Kailasanatha Temple (Kanchipuram) was also built by Narasimhavarman II.

question: As on February 2024, Yanthungo Patton is the Deputy Chief Minister of which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagaland.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As on February 2024, Yanthungo Patton (Y. Patton) was the Deputy Chief Minister of Nagaland. (नागालैंड के उप-मुख्यमंत्री — वाई. पैटन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Nagaland became a state on 1 December 1963; its capital is Kohima.

• Nagaland is famous for the Hornbill Festival (the "Festival of Festivals"), celebrated in December.

NOTE

• Nagaland is one of the "Seven Sisters" states of North-East India (Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, Meghalaya).

question: Which of the following is a mineral deficiency disease?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Goitre.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Goitre" is a mineral deficiency disease caused by the deficiency of iodine, leading to the swelling of the thyroid gland in the neck. (घेंघा रोग — आयोडीन की कमी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Rickets — caused by deficiency of Vitamin D (softening/weakening of bones).

• Scurvy — caused by deficiency of Vitamin C (bleeding gums).

• Marasmus — a form of protein-energy malnutrition in children.

NOTE

• Iodine is added to common salt (iodised salt) to prevent goitre. Other mineral-deficiency issues: anaemia (iron) and weak bones/teeth (calcium).

question: Sekrenyi festival of Nagaland is celebrated annually in the month of _______ as part of the Mini Hornbill Tribal Festival which is a celebration of purification accompanied with feasting and singing.
solution_text:
The correct answer is February.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Sekrenyi (Sekrenye) festival" of the Angami Naga tribe of Nagaland is celebrated annually in February. It is a festival of purification and sanctification, marked by feasting, singing and rituals. (सेक्रेनी महोत्सव — फरवरी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Sekrenyi" means "sanctification festival"; it is also called Phousanyi.

• Nagaland's biggest festival is the Hornbill Festival, held in December at Kisama.

NOTE

• Festivals of Nagaland: Sekrenyi (Angami), Moatsu (Ao), Tuluni (Sumi), Aoleang (Konyak) and the state-wide Hornbill Festival.

question: Purushottam Dadheech, a renowned Kathak dancer who had been honoured with Padma Shri award for 2020, is associated with which of the following places?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Purushottam Dadheech, a renowned Kathak dancer and guru honoured with the Padma Shri (2020), is associated with Madhya Pradesh (he is a leading exponent of the Kathak tradition and has trained many dancers). (पुरुषोत्तम दाधीच — मध्य प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• He is credited with popularising Kathak and blending it with other styles; he is associated with the Raigarh gharana tradition of Kathak.

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms, mainly of North and Central India.

NOTE

• Major Kathak gharanas: Lucknow, Jaipur, Banaras and Raigarh. Famous Kathak dancers: Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Kumudini Lakhia.

question: What does WFI stand for in the context of sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wrestling Federation of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the context of sports, "WFI" stands for the "Wrestling Federation of India", the national governing body for the sport of wrestling in India. (भारतीय कुश्ती महासंघ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The WFI is affiliated to the international wrestling body United World Wrestling (UWW).

• India has produced Olympic wrestling medallists such as Sushil Kumar, Yogeshwar Dutt, Sakshi Malik, Bajrang Punia and Ravi Kumar Dahiya.

NOTE

• Some sports federations for SSC: BCCI (cricket), AIFF (football), AITA (tennis), BAI (badminton), HI (hockey).

question: The architectural marvels, temples of Gangaikonda-Cholapuram, were built by which of the following king?
solution_text:
The correct answer is King Rajendra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The temples of Gangaikonda Cholapuram were built by the Chola king Rajendra I (Rajendra Chola I) to commemorate his victorious military campaign up to the Ganga river in the north. (गंगईकोंड चोलपुरम — राजेंद्र चोल प्रथम)

• The Brihadeeswarar (Gangaikonda Cholapuram) Temple is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (part of the "Great Living Chola Temples").

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Rajendra Chola I made Gangaikonda Cholapuram his new capital and took the title "Gangaikonda Chola" (the Chola who conquered the Ganga).

• The Cholas had a powerful navy and expanded their influence to Southeast Asia (Srivijaya).

NOTE

• Vijayalaya founded the Chola dynasty; Rajaraja I built the Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur. Mahendravarman was a Pallava king.

question: Which of the following is NOT an example of a 'Lagoon'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nainital.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Nainital" is a freshwater lake in the Kumaon Himalayas of Uttarakhand — it is NOT a lagoon. A lagoon is a shallow body of water separated from the sea by a sandbar or coral reef. (नैनीताल — झील, लैगून नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Chilika (Odisha) — the largest coastal lagoon in India (a brackish-water lagoon).

• Pulicat (Andhra Pradesh/Tamil Nadu) — the second-largest lagoon in India.

• Kolleru (Andhra Pradesh) — a large freshwater lake, often grouped with lagoons.

NOTE

• Lagoons are usually brackish (a mix of fresh and salt water) and are important habitats for birds and fish. Chilika is famous for migratory birds and Irrawaddy dolphins.

question: Dappu dance is a famous dance form of which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dappu" is a vigorous folk dance of Andhra Pradesh (and Telangana), performed to the beat of a percussion instrument called the "Dappu" (a frame drum). (डप्पू नृत्य — आंध्र प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Dappu dance is usually performed during festivals, fairs and processions, with energetic, synchronised movements.

• The classical dance of Andhra Pradesh is Kuchipudi.

NOTE

• Folk dances by state: Dappu (Andhra Pradesh), Bhangra/Giddha (Punjab), Chhau (Odisha/Jharkhand/Bengal), Garba (Gujarat), Bihu (Assam).

question: In its 279th report released in April 2023, the Law Commission of India has recommended the provision of which law to be retained?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sedition Law.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In its 279th report (April 2023), the Law Commission of India recommended that the Sedition Law (Section 124A of the Indian Penal Code) should be retained, with certain amendments and safeguards. (राजद्रोह कानून — 279वीं रिपोर्ट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Section 124A (IPC) deals with sedition — bringing hatred/contempt or exciting disaffection against the government by law. (In the new Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the provisions have been restructured.)

• The Law Commission of India is a non-statutory advisory body that recommends legal reforms to the government.

NOTE

• The sedition law was a subject of major debate regarding freedom of speech (Article 19(1)(a)) versus national security.

question: With reference to 'slash and burn' agriculture, which of the following names is NOT related to Odisha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Roca.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the given names for "slash and burn (shifting) agriculture", "Roca" is NOT related to Odisha — it is the term used in Brazil. The Odisha-related local names include Podu / Koman / Bringa / Pama Dabi. (रोका — ब्राज़ील, ओडिशा से संबंधित नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Local names of shifting cultivation in India: Jhum (North-East), Podu (Odisha/Andhra), Bewar/Dahiya (MP), Kumari (Western Ghats), Penda (Chhattisgarh).

• Around the world: Roca (Brazil), Milpa (Mexico/Central America), Ladang (Indonesia/Malaysia), Ray (Vietnam).

NOTE

• In slash-and-burn farming, forest patches are cleared and burnt, cultivated for a few years, then left fallow to regain fertility.

question: What was the amount earned by BCCI from the sale of five teams in the inaugural Women's Indian Premier League (WPL) in January 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is ₹4,669.99 crore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The BCCI earned about ₹4,669.99 crore from the sale of the five franchises (teams) of the inaugural Women's Premier League (WPL) in January 2023. (महिला प्रीमियर लीग — ₹4,669.99 करोड़)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The five WPL teams are based in Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Ahmedabad (Gujarat) and Lucknow.

• The first edition of the WPL (2023) was won by the Mumbai Indians (women).

NOTE

• The BCCI (Board of Control for Cricket in India) is the governing body for cricket in India; it also runs the men's IPL, one of the richest cricket leagues in the world.

question: Epilepsy is a disorder that affects which of the following parts of the human body?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brain cells.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Epilepsy is a neurological disorder that affects the brain (nerve cells/neurons). It is characterised by recurrent seizures (fits) caused by sudden, abnormal electrical activity in the brain. (मिर्गी — मस्तिष्क कोशिकाएँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Seizures may cause loss of consciousness, convulsions or unusual sensations.

• Epilepsy can often be controlled with medication; it is not contagious. This is a sensitive medical topic; the focus here is purely the factual organ affected.

NOTE

• The brain, spinal cord and nerves make up the nervous system. Other neurological conditions studied in exams include Parkinson's disease and Alzheimer's disease.

question: Which of the following options has all vector quantities?
option_1: Force, Velocity, Momentum, Energy and Power
option_2: Force, Velocity, Momentum, Energy and Acceleration
option_3: Power, Momentum, Energy, Speed and Work
option_4: Force, Velocity, Momentum, Weight and Acceleration
solution_text:
The correct answer is Force, Velocity, Momentum, Weight and Acceleration.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction. In Option 4, all five — Force, Velocity, Momentum, Weight and Acceleration — are vector quantities. (सदिश राशियाँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Energy, Power, Speed and Work are scalar quantities (they have only magnitude), so Options 1, 2 and 3 are wrong because each contains at least one scalar (Energy/Power/Speed/Work).

• "Weight" is a force (mass × gravitational acceleration) and is therefore a vector.

NOTE

• Examples of vectors: displacement, velocity, acceleration, force, momentum, weight.

• Examples of scalars: distance, speed, mass, time, energy, work, power, temperature.

question: National Rural Employment Guarantee Act was passed in which of the following years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2005.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA) was passed in 2005 (and came into force in 2006). It was later renamed the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) in 2009. (राष्ट्रीय ग्रामीण रोजगार गारंटी अधिनियम — 2005)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• MGNREGA guarantees at least 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.

• It is one of the world's largest social security / employment schemes and promotes the "Right to Work".

NOTE

• The scheme is demand-driven; if work is not provided within 15 days, the applicant is entitled to an unemployment allowance. It is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development.

question: According to Article _____, there shall be equality of opportunities for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment to any office under the State.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 16.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 16 of the Constitution guarantees equality of opportunity for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment to any office under the State. (अनुच्छेद 16 — लोक नियोजन में अवसर की समानता)

• It also allows reservation for backward classes not adequately represented in state services.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Article 14 — Equality before law; Article 15 — Prohibition of discrimination; Article 17 — Abolition of untouchability; Article 18 — Abolition of titles.

• Articles 14 to 18 together constitute the Right to Equality (Part III, Fundamental Rights).

NOTE

• Article 16 is a Fundamental Right and is enforceable in court. It ensures a fair and merit-based system for government jobs (with permitted reservations).

question: In the PM-SVANidhi Scheme (2020), the urban street vendors are eligible to avail a Working Capital Loan up to 10,000 with a tenure of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 year.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the PM SVANidhi Scheme (2020), urban street vendors can avail an initial collateral-free Working Capital Loan of up to ₹10,000, repayable within a tenure of 1 year (in monthly instalments). (पीएम स्वनिधि — 1 वर्ष की अवधि)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• On timely repayment, the vendor becomes eligible for higher loans of ₹20,000 and then ₹50,000.

• The scheme offers a 7% interest subsidy and incentives for digital transactions, and is run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

NOTE

• "SVANidhi" = PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi. It was launched during the COVID-19 pandemic to help street vendors resume their livelihoods.

question: Mica is which type of mineral?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Non-metallic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mica is a non-metallic mineral. It is an excellent electrical insulator with high dielectric strength, and is widely used in the electrical and electronics industry. (अभ्रक — अधात्विक खनिज)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India is a major producer of mica; major deposits are in Jharkhand, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan (the Koderma belt of Jharkhand is famous).

• Metallic minerals contain metals — ferrous (iron-based: iron ore, manganese) and non-ferrous (copper, bauxite, gold).

NOTE

• Non-metallic minerals include mica, limestone, gypsum, dolomite, salt and phosphate. Energy/fuel minerals include coal, petroleum and natural gas.

question: The model of 'Quasi Federal' form of government in Indian constitution is borrowed from which country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Canada.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The concept of a "Quasi-Federal" (strong Centre) form of government, along with the residuary powers being vested in the Centre and the appointment of State Governors by the Centre, was borrowed by the Indian Constitution from Canada. (कनाडा — अर्ध-संघीय व्यवस्था)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• From Canada, India also borrowed the idea of a Federation with a strong Centre and the advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.

• India is described as a "Union of States" (Article 1) — indestructible union with a strong central tilt.

NOTE

• Borrowed features: Fundamental Rights, Judicial Review (USA); Parliamentary system, Rule of Law (UK); Directive Principles (Ireland); Emergency provisions, Fundamental Duties (erstwhile USSR/others); Concurrent List (Australia).

question: Sahaswan gharana of Rampur was established by whom among the following personalities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ustad Inayat Hussain Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rampur-Sahaswan gharana of Hindustani classical (Khayal) vocal music was established/founded by Ustad Inayat Hussain Khan. (रामपुर-सहसवान घराना — उस्ताद इनायत हुसैन खान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Rampur-Sahaswan gharana is known for its clear voice production, rhythmic mastery and forceful taans.

• Famous exponents of this gharana include Ustad Mushtaq Hussain Khan, Ghulam Mustafa Khan and Rashid Khan.

NOTE

• Major Hindustani vocal gharanas: Gwalior (oldest), Agra, Kirana, Jaipur-Atrauli, Patiala, Mewati and Rampur-Sahaswan.

question: Which of the following social organisations was founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in 1875?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arya Samaj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in 1875 in Bombay (Mumbai). It was a Hindu reform movement that gave the call "Back to the Vedas" and opposed idol worship, casteism, child marriage and superstitions. (आर्य समाज — 1875, स्वामी दयानंद सरस्वती)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Swami Dayananda wrote "Satyarth Prakash (The Light of Truth)".

• The Arya Samaj promoted women's education, widow remarriage and the Shuddhi movement (reconversion). It set up DAV (Dayanand Anglo-Vedic) schools and colleges.

NOTE

• Other reform bodies: Brahmo Samaj (1828, Raja Ram Mohan Roy), Prarthana Samaj (1867, Atmaram Pandurang), Satyashodhak Samaj (1873, Jyotiba Phule).

question: The name of the autobiography of Saina Nehwal is called:
option_2: Playing to win, my life on and off court
solution_text:
The correct answer is Playing to win, my life on and off court.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The autobiography of the ace Indian badminton player Saina Nehwal is titled "Playing to Win: My Life On and Off Court". (साइना नेहवाल की आत्मकथा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Saina Nehwal was the first Indian woman to reach World No. 1 in badminton and won a bronze medal at the 2012 London Olympics. She has received the Padma Bhushan and the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna.

• "Unbreakable" is the autobiography of the boxer Mary Kom.

NOTE

• Sports autobiographies: "Playing It My Way" (Sachin Tendulkar), "The Race of My Life" (Milkha Singh), "Straight from the Heart" (Kapil Dev), "Ace Against Odds" (Sania Mirza).
